## Audit Checklist

| Requirement | Owning Patch(es) | Required Evidence | Review Posture |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prepared host identity is initialized before normal-session admission | `0044-oliphaunt-wasix-initialize-trusted-session-identity.patch` | `INIT_PG_TRUSTED_CLIENT`, `InitializeSessionUserId(username, useroid, false)`, `MyBackendType = B_BACKEND`, `MyProcPort->user_name = MemoryContextStrdup`, `IsNormalUserSession()`, `EventTriggerOnLogin();` | Consume the prepared capability in InitPostgres, not after bootstrap-superuser initialization. Enforce catalog login/database policy, role defaults and login triggers without pretending HBA authentication occurred; unprepared recovery remains standalone. |
| Fixed JSONB constructor metadata preserves PostgreSQL semantics | `0043-oliphaunt-wasix-cache-jsonb-build-object-metadata.patch` | `JsonbBuildObjectState`, `get_fn_expr_variadic`, `FirstNormalObjectId`, `jsonb_build_object_cache_drop_cast` | Ordinary calls reuse immutable expression metadata; explicit VARIADIC arrays keep the generic path and user-defined types are recategorized so cast DDL remains visible. |
| WASIX WAL durability exposes only explicit sync operations | `0042-oliphaunt-wasix-use-explicit-wal-sync-operations.patch` | `PLATFORM_DEFAULT_WAL_SYNC_METHOD`, `WAL_SYNC_METHOD_FDATASYNC`, `OLIPHAUNT_WASM_EXPLICIT_WAL_SYNC_ONLY`, `explicit fd_datasync operation` | The shared PostgreSQL port selects fdatasync and removes open_sync/open_datasync from the WASIX GUC choices because Wasmer does not honor their open flags. |
| WASIX dynamic-main build spine is isolated | `0001-oliphaunt-wasix-add-wasix-dl-build-spine.patch` | `PORTNAME), wasix-dl`, `oliphaunt: $(OBJS)` | Build plumbing lands before lifecycle behavior, so linker changes are reviewable alone. |
| Backend protocol I/O is host-owned without touching normal sockets | `0002-oliphaunt-wasix-add-backend-host-io-hooks.patch` | `OliphauntWasmHostIO`, `secure_raw_read`, `secure_raw_write` | Only OLIPHAUNT_WASM_SINGLE_USER installs the callback table. |
| Startup packet parsing remains PostgreSQL-owned | `0003-oliphaunt-wasix-export-startup-packet-parser.patch` | `ProcessStartupPacket`, `OLIPHAUNT_WASM_HOST_EXPORT("ProcessStartupPacket")` | The host can call the parser, but PostgreSQL still validates the startup packet. |
| Host lifecycle exports stay explicit | `0004-oliphaunt-wasix-add-host-lifecycle-exports.patch` | `oliphaunt_wasix_start`, `oliphaunt_wasix_pq_flush`, `oliphaunt_wasix_get_proc_port` | Host-visible entry points are named exports instead of broad syscall remaps. |
| Protocol loop recovery remains inside a live PostgreSQL boundary | `0005-oliphaunt-wasix-add-loop-pumped-protocol-exports.patch`, `0019-oliphaunt-wasix-schedule-ready-after-loop-step-recovery.patch` | `PostgresMainLoopOnce`, `OLIPHAUNT_WASM_MAIN_LOOP_RECOVERED`, `OLIPHAUNT_WASM_MAIN_LOOP_INPUT_ENDED`, `PG_exception_stack = NULL`, `send_ready_for_query = true` | Each host-pumped step owns a live call-site exception boundary, returns a typed outcome, and clears the boundary before returning. |
| COPY protocol state is host-observable | `0006-oliphaunt-wasix-report-copy-protocol-state.patch`, `0008-oliphaunt-wasix-reset-copy-state-on-error-recovery.patch` | `oliphaunt_wasix_protocol_report_copy_response`, `OLIPHAUNT_WASIX_PROTOCOL_COPY_NONE` | COPY state is reported and cleared around PostgreSQL error recovery. |
| PGXS side modules and backend ThinLTO use the WASIX dynamic-link contract | `0007-oliphaunt-wasix-add-wasix-pgxs-side-module-support.patch`, `0022-oliphaunt-wasix-use-wasm-ld-for-backend-core.patch` | `PGXS`, `WASM_LD ?= $(shell $(CC) -print-prog-name=wasm-ld)`, `WASM_LTO_SJLJ_FLAGS`, `-mllvm --wasm-enable-eh`, `-mllvm --wasm-enable-sjlj`, `-mllvm --wasm-use-legacy-eh=false`, `-mllvm --exception-model=wasm` | Extension modules use the dynamic-link contract, and the backend relocatable ThinLTO boundary performs the same complete EH/SJLJ lowering as the sealed final link. |
| Process identity and shared memory stay behind the port header | `0009-oliphaunt-wasix-route-process-identity-through-port.patch`, `0010-oliphaunt-wasix-route-sysv-shmem-through-port.patch`, `0011-oliphaunt-wasix-prefer-posix-semaphores.patch` | `oliphaunt_wasix_geteuid`, `oliphaunt_wasix_shmget`, `PREFERRED_SEMAPHORES=UNNAMED_POSIX` | WASIX platform gaps are explicit port-layer dependencies, not scattered runtime guesses. |
| Tool/runtime platform stubs fail closed | `0021-oliphaunt-wasix-declare-wasix-fork.patch`, `0025-oliphaunt-wasix-stub-pg-dump-parallel-fork.patch`, `0032-oliphaunt-wasix-treat-directory-fsync-eisdir-as-unsupported.patch` | `fork_process`, `oliphaunt_wasix_pgdump_fork`, `errno == EISDIR` | Unavailable WASIX behavior is explicit and narrow instead of silently emulated. |
| XLog-size checkpoint pressure is deferred to a transaction-free safe point | `0027-oliphaunt-wasix-defer-xlog-size-checkpoint-requests.patch` | `oliphaunt_wasix_checkpoint_deferred = true;`, `OliphauntWasixPerformDeferredCheckpoint(void)`, `RequestCheckpoint(CHECKPOINT_CAUSE_XLOG);`, `oliphaunt_wasix_checkpoint_deferred = false;`, `upstream
RequestCheckpoint already performs the requested checkpoint locally` | XLogWrite records pressure but cannot recurse into checkpointing. ReadyForQuery services it after the transaction boundary, failures retain the pending flag, and truthful standalone topology selects PostgreSQL's local RequestCheckpoint path. |
| Controlled initdb collation discovery | `0033-oliphaunt-wasix-control-initdb-collation-discovery.patch` | `OLIPHAUNT_INTERNAL_ICU_READY`, `OLIPHAUNT_INTERNAL_SKIP_SYSTEM_COLLATION_DISCOVERY`, `OLIPHAUNT_INTERNAL_SKIP_ICU_DISCOVERY`, `strcmp`, `pg_collation_actual_version`, `pg_import_system_collations` | Public collation import retains PostgreSQL semantics. Distributed standard seeds suppress OS and ICU discovery; ICU seeds suppress only OS discovery and verify ICU readiness for initdb's unicode-version probe. |
| Ordinary and COPY streaming keep explicit mode-separated transport ABI | `0034-oliphaunt-wasix-declare-hybrid-protocol-transport.patch` | `oliphaunt_wasix_set_protocol_transport(int mode)`, `oliphaunt_wasix_protocol_stream_active(void)` | Finite ordinary requests use buffered input with streamed output, while interactive COPY keeps a separate hybrid duplex transition; Rust and TypeScript provide bounded adapters over the same guest ABI. |
| WASIX strong randomness fails closed without descriptor or buffered-state pressure | `0037-oliphaunt-wasix-use-checked-getrandom.patch` | `#elif defined(__wasi__)`, `#include <sys/random.h>`, `res = getrandom(p, len, 0);`, `if (errno == EINTR)`, `if (res == 0)`, `No guest-side state to initialize or duplicate.` | Every no-OpenSSL WASIX backend bypasses the virtual random device, preserves entropy failures, and keeps no lifecycle-sensitive entropy reservoir. |
| Unsupported writeback hints stay separate from real durability | `0038-oliphaunt-wasix-disable-unsupported-writeback-hints.patch` | `#if defined(OLIPHAUNT_WASM_SINGLE_USER)`, `Actual fsync/fdatasync durability remains enabled.`, `#elif defined(HAVE_SYNC_FILE_RANGE)` | The single-backend guest omits only pg_flush_data hints that WASIX rejects on read-only descriptors; PostgreSQL fsync and fdatasync remain active. |
| PostgreSQL modules own their SJLJ catch frames | `0039-oliphaunt-wasix-inline-sigsetjmp.patch` | `-DOLIPHAUNT_WASM_SIDE_MODULE`, `WebAssembly SJLJ requires setjmp to be visible at the protected call site.`, `defined(OLIPHAUNT_WASM_SINGLE_USER) || defined(OLIPHAUNT_WASM_SIDE_MODULE)`, `#undef sigsetjmp`, `#define sigsetjmp(env, savesigs) ((void) (savesigs), setjmp(env))` | PG_TRY expands to a compiler-recognized setjmp in the main executable and every PostgreSQL side module, so nested errors unwind to the live module-local handler. |
| Standalone WASIX libpq sockets are actually nonblocking | `0040-oliphaunt-wasix-set-libpq-sockets-nonblocking.patch` | `defined(SOCK_NONBLOCK) && !defined(__wasi__)`, `!defined(SOCK_NONBLOCK) || defined(__wasi__)`, `pg_set_noblock(conn->sock)` | WASIX uses PostgreSQL's existing fcntl fallback because Wasmer ignores socket type flags; native platforms retain upstream atomic socket creation. |
| Captured Oliphaunt psql scripts remain noninteractive | `0041-oliphaunt-wasix-honor-noninteractive-psql-invocations.patch` | `OLIPHAUNT_PSQL_NONINTERACTIVE`, `strcmp(oliphaunt_noninteractive, "1") == 0`, `!isatty(fileno(stdin)) || !isatty(fileno(stdout))` | Only the private exact-value marker overrides virtual terminal detection; ordinary WASIX psql retains upstream isatty semantics. |
| Trusted embedded lifecycle preserves truthful standalone topology | `0029-oliphaunt-wasix-model-trusted-embedded-session.patch` | `OLIPHAUNT_TRUSTED_EMBEDDED_UNSELECTED`, `OLIPHAUNT_TRUSTED_EMBEDDED_PREPARED`, `OLIPHAUNT_TRUSTED_EMBEDDED_ATTACHED`, `return trusted_embedded_lifecycle ==`, `reached_main ||`, `ConfigurePreparedTrustedEmbeddedSession(void)`, `SetConfigOption("io_method", "sync", PGC_POSTMASTER, PGC_S_OVERRIDE)`, `SetConfigOption("max_worker_processes", "0", PGC_POSTMASTER,`, `AttachPreparedTrustedEmbeddedSession(void)`, `if (!AttachPreparedTrustedEmbeddedSession())`, `IsNormalUserSession(void)`, `if (IsUnderPostmaster)`, `!IsTrustedEmbeddedSession() && pathkeys == NIL`, `ERRCODE_FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED`, `IsUnderPostmaster excludes the trusted embedded session's synthetic fd.` | Preparation is inactive, attach is one-shot, guest GUC limits apply before shared-memory sizing, positive catalog and DDL semantics are explicit, and worker or postmaster-only paths retain upstream standalone fail-closed behavior. |

## Experiment Patch Disposition

| Experiment Patch | Status | WASIX Runtime Decision | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0001-wasix-use-posix-dsm-not-sysv.patch` | `not-carried` | replaced where relevant by 0010 and 0011 | The experiment patch changes full-concurrent PostgreSQL dynamic shared memory selection. The embedded WASIX runtime does not take postmaster DSM as a product constraint; it instead routes SysV shmem through the wasix-dl port header and explicitly selects POSIX semaphores. |
| `0003-wasix-libpq-static-encoding-shim.patch` | `covered-by-build-spine` | covered by the WASIX bridge aliases and standalone pg_dump build path | The released-lane bridge already provides weak pg_char_to_encoding and pg_encoding_to_char aliases for static pg_dump/libpq linkage. No PG18 source patch is needed unless a future configured build proves a tool-specific gap. |
| `0004-wasix-core-execbackend-initdb-runtime.patch` | `not-carried` | full-concurrent runtime blocker patch, not embedded product shape | The patch addresses EXEC_BACKEND, fork/exec, root checks, locale command probing, and directory fsync behavior for proper concurrent PostgreSQL under WASIX. The embedded WASIX runtime avoids the postmaster/fork lifecycle; any tool blocker found later should become a smaller tool-specific patch. |
| `0005-pg-dump-avoid-lto-executequery-collision.patch` | `ported` | ported as 0018-oliphaunt-wasix-avoid-pg-dump-executequery-lto-collision.patch | This is a narrow pg_dump source hygiene patch that supports standalone WASIX tool builds under thin LTO without changing query behavior. |
| `0006-like-literal-substring-fast-path.patch` | `removed-after-correctness-review` | removed from the applied series; patch number 0024 remains reserved for traceability | The bytewise substring search could begin and end inside characters in non-UTF8 multibyte encodings, changing valid LIKE results. The optimization objective remains an experiment until an encoding-aware design has cross-encoding differential evidence and isolated material performance evidence. |
| `0007-top-xid-current-transaction-fast-path.patch` | `removed-after-evidence-review` | removed from the applied series; patch number 0015 remains reserved for traceability | The PG18 port's early false result is semantically plausible because it runs only after the top-XID comparison fails and only when parallel XIDs, parent states, aborted state, and child XIDs are absent. Correctness alone does not earn a hot-path fork from PostgreSQL: neither the experiment nor the retained reports contain a factor-isolated profile or A/B showing a material gain. Restore TransactionIdIsCurrentTransactionId to upstream. Reopen only if an alternating retained-binary screen dominated by current-transaction tuple visibility shows a material repeatable removal regression, then carry differential aborted, nested, parallel, and prepared-transaction tests with the experiment. |
| `0008-btree-int4-compare-fast-path.patch` | `removed-after-correctness-review` | removed from the applied series; patch number 0016 remains reserved for traceability | The relation opfamily and int4 input type do not prove that the active scan support function is PostgreSQL's built-in btint4cmp; a user-defined opclass can belong to that family. Bypassing FunctionCall2Coll could therefore change index ordering semantics. Any retry must prove the exact comparator identity and earn its place with isolated performance evidence. |
| `0009-btree-delete-stack-state.patch` | `removed-after-design-review` | removed from the applied series; patch number 0017 remains reserved for traceability | The patch moved about 19 KiB of page-local B-tree deletion scratch from PostgreSQL memory contexts to each Wasm stack frame without isolated performance evidence. That worsened the failure boundary from a recoverable allocation error to a possible Wasm stack trap and silently changed the table-AM allocation contract. Preserve allocator-churn reduction as an experiment; any retry must first prove a material isolated win and retain explicit, recoverable ownership. |
| `0010-btree-bottomup-delete-runtime-toggle.patch` | `rejected-for-default-lane` | diagnostic toggle was tested with Oliphaunt env names but not kept in the patch stack | Disabling bottom-up deletion changes PostgreSQL's index maintenance behavior. A local PG18 WASIX port of the diagnostic hook made the default release-profile 9/10 run much slower before any override was enabled, so it is not a defensible carried patch. |
| `0011-btree-first-int4-compare-fast-path.patch` | `removed-after-correctness-review` | removed from the applied series; patch number 0026 remains reserved for traceability | This companion inherited the same unproven comparator-identity assumption as patch 0016 and additionally bypassed PostgreSQL's attribute extraction path. Restoring the upstream comparison path is correct and keeps the optimization available only as a future isolated experiment. |
| `0012-hash-bytes-unaligned-load-fast-path.patch` | `removed-after-toolchain-review` | removed from the applied series; patch number 0014 remains reserved for traceability | With the selected WASIX clang 21.1.2 at -O2, both PostgreSQL's upstream four-byte shift expression and the patch's memcpy helper lower to the same unaligned i32.load 0:p2align=0. The patch duplicates both hash_bytes tail switches and changes only some 4-byte and 8-byte tail code shape, without isolated A/B evidence that this residual difference is material. Restore the smaller upstream implementation. Reopen only if an alternating retained-binary hash workload shows a material repeatable removal regression; any retry should target the proven residual code shape instead of duplicating the complete switch. |
| `0035-oliphaunt-wasix-use-single-backend-spinlocks.patch` | `removed-after-evidence-review` | removed from the applied series; patch number 0035 remains reserved for traceability | PR #133 introduced 0035 together with 0036 to replace guest atomic read-modify-write spinlocks under a one-backend-per-instance assumption. Current public placements are normally single-owner: TypeScript selects the immutable SingleProgram host policy, Rust denies additional guest Wasm tasks, reusable modules are instantiated with fresh stores and memories, and public execution handles require mutable ownership. That topology evidence makes the idea plausible but does not earn a backend-wide synchronization rewrite: PR #133 and the retained benchmark reports contain no factor-isolated A/B for either patch, and the host policy only denies guest-created execution rather than itself proving every callback reentry, signal, environment clone/reinit, journal restore, and side-module observer path. Restore the normal PostgreSQL spinlock path instead of maintaining containment for an unmeasured optimization. Reopen only as a coupled experiment with 0036 if alternating retained-binary Node runs show a material, repeatable removal regression and adversarial equivalence closes every observer path. |
| `0036-oliphaunt-wasix-specialize-single-backend-atomics.patch` | `removed-after-evidence-review` | removed from the applied series; patch number 0036 remains reserved for traceability | PR #133 introduced 0036 with 0035 to replace every PostgreSQL backend flag, uint32, uint64, fence, and read-modify-write operation with volatile scalar accesses. It preserved the public layouts and sequential compare-exchange result contract, but also asserted 8-byte single-copy atomicity and made the optimization depend on exclusive ownership across Rust AOT, all TypeScript placements, host callbacks, signals, side modules, and Wasmer clone/reinit/restore behavior. The immutable SingleProgram policy and Rust task gate substantially improve the normal topology, yet there is no factor-isolated A/B showing that this broad semantic risk buys material speed. Restore the normal PostgreSQL atomic path. Reopen only as a coupled experiment with 0035 after profiling identifies atomic instructions as material, alternating retained-binary Node runs reproduce a removal regression, and adversarial tests prove execution and observer exclusivity. |
| `historical-0035-oliphaunt-wasix-avoid-xlogwrite-prevseg-division.patch` | `removed-after-evidence-review` | removed from the applied series; patch number 0030 remains reserved for traceability | The cached exclusive segment end wrapped to zero for the final uint64 WAL segment. Unsigned distance from a cached segment start can repair that invariant without division, and the retained property test proves it against PostgreSQL's PrevLogSegNo arithmetic for every valid segment size and uint64 endpoints. Correctness does not earn the optimization: the only focused target regressed COMMIT from 13.993 ms to 15.603 ms, while the claimed full-suite improvement lacks an isolated per-patch table and is confounded by artifact and run changes. Reopen only as a new experiment if a factor-isolated, repeatable COMMIT screen shows a material removal regression. |
| `runtime-0013-fail-active-portals-on-host-recovery.patch` | `removed-after-architecture-review` | removed from the applied series; patch number 0013 remains reserved for traceability | The patch compensated for a force-all host recovery path that skipped arbitrary nested PG_TRY/PG_CATCH cleanup. Marking active portals failed repaired one observed symptom but could not restore every skipped handler. The main module now expands sigsetjmp at each protected call site, so PortalRun's own live PG_CATCH marks the portal failed before rethrowing to the typed top-level step boundary. |
| `runtime-0020-rearm-exception-stack-after-host-recovery.patch` | `removed-after-correctness-review` | removed from the applied series; patch number 0020 remains reserved for traceability | The patch assigned PG_exception_stack to PostgresMain's saved buffer after the _start export had already unwound, leaving a pointer to a returned WebAssembly frame. Each typed PostgresMainLoopOnce call now establishes its own live call-site boundary and clears PG_exception_stack before every return; no boundary is retained across host calls. |

## Guardrails

- `source.toml` patch series exactly matches the patch directory.
- Every patch has a deterministic `From: Oliphaunt Maintainers <dev@oliphaunt.dev>` header.
- Every patch has a deterministic `Subject: [PATCH] oliphaunt-wasix: ...` header and a rationale before the diff.
- Added PostgreSQL lines are checked for trailing whitespace and space-before-tab indentation.
- Changed upstream files must exactly match the expected touchpoint table above; new upstream touchpoints need an explicit rationale before landing.
- Required audit checks prove their evidence in the named owning patch or patches.
- Experiment patches can only be ported, rejected, or replaced with a recorded WASIX runtime decision and rationale.
